newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross reunites 8,000 lost Rwandan children.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross reunites 8,000 lost Rwandan children.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross said on Thursday it had reunited three-quarters of 10,500 lost Rwandan Hutu refugee children with their families who lost them during their mass influx from Zaire and Tanzania.
The children were separated from their parents when half a million Rwandan Hutus in Tanzania were expelled by troops in December and 600,000 returned home from east Zaire.

The ICRC's computer tracing programme in Rwanda for children is the largest since World War Two and has registered names of more than 80,000 children so far -- among 100,000 of whom were lost or orphaned during Rwanda's 1994 Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis.
The programme is assisted by radio broadcasts, Polaroid photos of children and parents, and messages delivered by ICRC.
